prompt:
Create a complete neutral rough monochrome film storyboard page on white paper: exactly 12 clearly separated panels arranged in 3 columns and 4 rows, read left to right and top to bottom. Each panel is a portrait 9:16 camera composition. Pencil/charcoal contour sketches only, unpolished production planning. Human silhouettes have ordinary simplified human head and torso proportions, NOT round-head stick figures, NOT whiteboard glyphs, NOT polished ChronoStick production art. No color, photorealism, final costume design, source logos or detailed face likeness. The wooden-boy puppet prop has a short nose, small cap and visible elbow/knee joints. Cinema/studio/dock equipment fits the early 1940s. No readable text inside the scenes. Put only the exact planning panel IDs in each panel margin. Every panel must depict its own composition, do not merge or omit panels. Maintain the same simple producer silhouette where he recurs.

S13: Close training drawing. One plain human hand draws a simple WWII propeller-aircraft silhouette on paper; no puppet, no text.
S14: Wide training projection. A projected aircraft silhouette fills a plain screen; projector at bottom edge; no people.
S15: Medium serviceman viewing. Exactly one seated serviceman watches that aircraft training image; no battle or crowd.
S16: Medium studio work. Exactly one suited producer sets a film canister beside a blank document on a desk; modest work, no cash pile.
S17: Close canister handoff. Two plain human hands exchange a single round film canister; bodies remain outside frame.
S18: Close ticket exchange. One ticket-seller hand passes one unprinted ticket to one patron hand at a booth; no numbers or words.
S19: Medium audience seats. Exactly two people, one adult and one child, settle into cinema seats looking toward the screen; no implied packed house.
S20: Close projector start. One projector casts a bright beam toward a screen; no people.
S21: Medium movie screen. The short-nosed wooden-boy puppet stands on a cinema screen; no numbers, slogan, wartime costume or combat.
S22: Close child watching. Exactly one child in profile watches the light from the screen with quiet interest; no detailed likeness.
S23: Close projected puppet. Closer view of the same projected wooden puppet, a calm friendly expression and short nose.
S24: Wide resolved cinema. Back view of exactly one adult and one child seated together, looking at a steady puppet projection; settled ending.

This is internal composition planning for an approximately 30-second historical Short. Clear primary props, exact visible subject counts, one simple action per panel; no decorative additions.
